subject: Diagnosing HMC/NUTS sampler, sampler parameters, manuals, shinyStan, (feature suggestions)

messages.author: 3f37be0cf708d442
messages.subject: Diagnosing HMC/NUTS sampler, sampler parameters, manuals, shinyStan, (feature suggestions)
parts:
Dear stan users and developers,

I am currently trying to improve model estimation by modifying some sampler parameters. Here are a few suggestions about how this could be made easier from the perspective of a user.
(Note that I am using “sampler parameter” both for the user-settable parameters like max_treedepth and for the parameters reported like treedepth)

In short:

1)      Consolidate and improve description of key sampler parameters that should be investigated or could be changed by the user
2)      Be clearer about which aspect (pre/post warmup, distribution, mean, max?) of the reported sampler parameters is most relevant
3)      Show sampler parameters  when using print(stanfit) in rstan
4)      Where to find sampler parameter in a stanfit object
5)      Show distributions of sampler parameters and parameter settings in shiny stan


In detail:

1) Sampler parameter description

From browsing through and reading in the the cmdstan guide, the stan reference, and the rstan manual I got the impression that the sampler parameters a less unexperienced user (like me) might want to play with are the target acceptance rate, jittering of step size, and maximum treedepth.

I found the description of these parameters in the cmdstan manual the clearest. The stan reference does not seem to detail default parameters values, and rstan manual does not do a lot of explaining. I think the reader could benefit if there would be only one description (I’d prefer in the stan reference), to which the other manuals point at a prominent place.

One thing I think would also help is to have a brief discussion of these key parameters together, in addition to their description in section for HMC and nuts parameters respectively. This joint discussion could also suggest which parameters one could try to change first (if this can be said) and describe how they interact in their effect on acceptance rate, estimation time etc.


2) Which aspects of the sampler parameters should one check?

From Michael B.’s recent post on the list I infer that one should examine the entire distribution of the treedepth parameter. I am not sure if this is also said so in the manuals. Maybe one could add/highlight this point? In this context it would also be good to know what constitutes a “bad” distribution. Is it ok when 0, 1, 5, 10 or how many percent of the samples reach the maximum tree depth? Should I be more interested in the warmup or the sampling period.


3) Sampler parameter statistics in print(stanfit)

That works nicely in cmdstan and it would be nice to also have it in rstan (I haven’t use pystan).


4) Which sampler parameters were used?

Maybe I am only overlooking this, but I couldn’t find where in the stanfit object the sampler parameters used are stored (e.g.  max_treedepth, adapt_delta, …).


5) Sampler parameters in shinyStan

The diagnosis tab of shinyStan is very useful. I think it would be even more useful if the sub-tab HMC/NUTS would also show which sampler parameters were used for the current model, and if, following Michael B.’s point, it would show distributions in addition to or instead of the stats. A reference to the section of the stan reference in which the sampler parameters are explained in more detail would also be helpful (or just copy paste the entire section, which would be the most user friendly).

Related, it would be nice if the tab that shows trace plot also had a pop-up window in which feature of “bad” chains are described.

I realize that these are things the user should know, but if shinyStan is thought as a way to make stan as accessible as possible to new users, collecting all information needed to evaluate the model in one place is a useful.


Cheers - Guido

Hi Guido, your suggestions for shinyStan are great. Thanks!

I made a few comments below.

On Wednesday, March 4, 2015 at 8:52:52 AM UTC-5, Guido Biele wrote:

5) Sampler parameters in shinyStan

The diagnosis tab of shinyStan is very useful. I think it would be even more useful if the sub-tab HMC/NUTS would also show which sampler parameters were used for the current model, and if, following Michael B.’s point, it would show distributions in addition to or instead of the stats.
I'm not sure I'd want to remove the stats, but I definitely think adding the distributions is a good idea.

A reference to the section of the stan reference in which the sampler parameters are explained in more detail would also be helpful (or just copy paste the entire section, which would be the most user friendly).

Yeah, right now the glossary section in shinyStan is pretty thin for the sampler parameters (i.e. one sentence definitions). I'd like to fill this out with more details and/or links to more detailed discussions.
Related, it would be nice if the tab that shows trace plot also had a pop-up window in which feature of “bad” chains are described.

We should definitely give an idea as to what to look for. It can sometimes be tricky to give widely applicable advice, but I think with trace plots there are certainly general suggestions that can be made.

I realize that these are things the user should know, but if shinyStan is thought as a way to make stan as accessible as possible to new users, collecting all information needed to evaluate the model in one place is a useful.
I couldn't agree more! We're just getting started with shinyStan, so feedback like yours is incredibly valuable. Thanks!
